method: Perception-aligned data layer (pseudo ground truth + verifiable visual facts) and process-aligned optimisation: hierarchical reward fusion with a process-aware score inside V-GRPO.
data: Process-aware reasoning data built by their pipeline; Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone.
evaluation: HallusionBench, MMStar, MMMU, MathVista, MathVerse (vision-only subset); baselines: base model, base+GRPO.
findings: Reduces reasoning hallucinations; state-of-the-art on HallusionBench while keeping MMMU/MathVista/MathVerse.
limitations: Authors: bounded by base-model perception; exact-match reward penalises semantically equivalent wording.
reference: Y. Li, Q. Hui, C. Yan, et al., "PaLMR: Towards Faithful Visual Reasoning via Multimodal Process Alignment," arXiv:2603.06652, 2026. [CVPR 2026 Findings, pp. 6114-6124, doi:10.1109/CVPRF71909.2026.00587]

method: Perceval: a trained process reward model that extracts image-related claims, checks each against the image and returns hallucinated spans; token-level advantages in GRPO; also used for test-time truncation and regeneration.
data: Perception-intensive supervised data to train Perceval (sizes not extracted).
evaluation: Benchmarks from several domains with RL-trained reasoning VLMs; baselines include VLM-R1 and LMM-R1; majority voting for test-time scaling.
findings: Gains on several benchmarks across reasoning VLMs; better than majority voting for test-time scaling.
limitations: Authors: not stated as a section; it needs a separately trained reward model (reviewer note).
reference: Y. Min, K. Zhou, Y. Li, et al., "Improving Vision-language Models with Perception-centric Process Reward Models," arXiv:2604.24583, 2026. [CVPR 2026, pp. 33099-33109 (DBLP listing)]

method: Lightweight plug-and-play consistency reward model + Hybrid Reward Advantage Splitting (HRAS) in GRPO.
data: Training sets: PuzzleVQA-style set (6.5K), Math-40K, CV-Bench training data; several Qwen LVLMs.
evaluation: In-domain PuzzleVQA; out-of-domain AlgoPuzzleVQA, CVBench, MathVision, MathVista; baseline: standard GRPO.
findings: Improves task performance and reduces thinking-answer inconsistency; more faithful traces.
limitations: Authors: only models up to 7B tested; image-text only, no video.
reference: J. Cao, Z. Lu, X. Sun, et al., "CORA: Analyzing and bridging thinking-answer gap in Multimodal RLVR via Consistency- Oriented Reasoning Alignment," arXiv:2606.14691, 2026. [Preprint (submitted to EMNLP 2026)]

contribution: VLM description reward plus reasoning SFT
method: PeRL-VL: VLM-based description reward scoring self-generated descriptions for faithfulness and sufficiency; text-only Reasoning SFT stage.
data: Logic-rich CoT data (e.g. OpenThought) for SFT; Qwen2.5-VL-7B base.
evaluation: VLMEvalKit benchmarks incl. OCRBench, MathVista_MINI; Pass@1; baselines: standard RLVR, text-only SFT, GPT-4o distillation.
findings: Average Pass@1 63.3% to 68.8%; beats standard RLVR.
limitations: Not stated as a section; uses an extra multimodal judge model (reviewer note).
reference: H. A. Just, Y. Fan, H. Zhao, et al., "More Than the Final Answer: Improving Visual Extraction and Logical Consistency in Vision-Language Models," arXiv:2512.12487, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Cross-modal counterfactual regulariser: maximise the gap between predictions and a state with critical visual cues suppressed; plugs into GRPO/DAPO; no external reward model.
data: Standard multimodal RL training data (e.g. Geo3K-style sets); sizes not extracted.
evaluation: MMMU-Pro vision, Geo3K, We-Math, MMK12, MathVerse, LogicVista; baselines: GRPO/DAPO and PAPO.
findings: +3.17 to +6.25% over standard RL baselines; +1.32 to +2.13% over PAPO.
limitations: Authors: extra computational cost (Appendix B).
reference: Z. Yu, W. Sun, G. Yang, et al., "CFPO: Counterfactual Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2606.23206, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: ICML 2026)]

method: Token-level causal-completeness reward and a causally informed advantage inside GRPO.
data: Not clearly extracted.
evaluation: Several benchmarks incl. a high-resolution factual/captioning benchmark; baselines not clearly extracted.
findings: Reports gains across benchmarks (abstract gives no numbers).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: P. Guo, J. Wang, W. Qiang, et al., "COPO: Causal-Oriented Policy Optimization for Hallucinations of MLLMs," arXiv:2508.04182, 2025. [Preprint]

method: EASE: evidence-region annotations become a visual-token attention target used as process supervision on high-reward trajectories only.
data: Training set with single- and multi-region evidence annotations; Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-4B/8B.
evaluation: Perception, hallucination, visual-math and multimodal-reasoning benchmarks; baseline: DAPO.
findings: +2.5 to +3.1 average points over DAPO on three backbones.
limitations: Authors: needs evidence annotations (box construction cost); suited to localisable evidence.
reference: R. Hu, C. Wang, L. Wei, et al., "Attend to Evidence: Evidence-Anchored Spatial Attention Supervision for Multimodal RLVR," arXiv:2605.30912, 2026. [Findings of EMNLP 2026, pp. 4295-4313, doi:10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.204]

method: Anchoring (attention supervised against image regions) + Reinforcing (counterfactual image intervention rewards trajectories that rely on vision).
data: Region annotations from an automated annotator (Gemini-3-Flash); Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
evaluation: MathVision, MathVerse, MathVista, WeMath, DynaMath, MMMU-Pro, HallusionBench; recent multimodal reasoning baselines.
findings: Outperforms recent baselines on both backbones with less training data.
limitations: Authors: region annotations and extra masked-image forward pass.
reference: C. Tian, Z. Lu, H. Liu, et al., "Faithful-MR1: Faithful Multimodal Reasoning via Anchoring and Reinforcing Visual Attention," arXiv:2605.22072, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Atomic-proposition rubrics scoring Visual Faithfulness, Reasoning Consistency and Instruction Following; prefix-localised credit in GRPO.
data: V-Rubrics 50K built from 17 sources and annotated with Gemini-3-Pro; SFT on OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K; Qwen3-VL-8B.
evaluation: Multimodal benchmarks; baselines: shared SFT checkpoint and answer-only GRPO.
findings: Beats SFT and answer-only GRPO; largest gains on knowledge-oriented and visually grounded benchmarks.
limitations: Authors: rubric quality and judge verification; approximate prefix-credit localisation.
reference: S. Tian, M. Li, Y. Dong, et al., "V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning," arXiv:2608.25580, 2026. [EMNLP 2026 main, pp. 35524-35543, doi:10.18653/2026.emnlp-main.1558]

method: Confidence-augmented outputs and a GRPO objective that penalises calibration error and poor abstention; confidence used at inference to revisit evidence.
data: 50K LLaVA-Instruct samples reformatted; pseudo-labelled confidences; InternVL3-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B.
evaluation: POPE, HallusionBench, AMBER, MMHal-Bench; MME and MMBench for general ability; Expected Calibration Error; baselines: DPO and decoding.
findings: Lower hallucination and lower ECE than DPO and decoding baselines.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Z. Ding, Z. Zhao, Y. He, et al., "SAVOR: Self-Aware Visual Grounding via Confidence-Calibrated Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation," arXiv:2609.16601, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: ICONIP 2026)]

method: Semantic-entropy-triggered expert prefixes plus advantage-sign-aware Renyi preconditioning.
data: Prefixes from dataset traces or verified rollouts; four training seeds.
evaluation: POPE, VideoHallucer, HallusionBench; MMBench, MMStar, VideoMMMU; baselines: GRPO and frozen models.
findings: Both branches beat GRPO; interaction significant on VideoMMMU (+4.0).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Y. Zhuang, M. Pan, W. Gan, et al., "DEEPO: Dual-Entropy Enhanced Policy Optimization for Hallucination in MLLMs," arXiv:2609.28570, 2026. [Preprint]

venue_note: Springer LNCS, pp. 287-305, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37232-1_16 (arXiv comment: ECCV 2026)
method: VIGIL: RL post-training that maximises visual-response mutual information and penalises blind confidence under attention masking.
data: Preference data (uses 25% of the data of state-of-the-art methods).
evaluation: Hallucination and reasoning benchmarks, MMLU and GSM8K for text-only retention; baselines: alignment methods incl. DPO.
findings: Beats recent alignment methods with 25% of the data; models 7B-72B.
limitations: Authors: counterfactual built by zero-out masking only.
reference: X. Xiao, C. Liu, C. Liao, et al., "Staying VIGILant: Mitigating Visual Laziness via Counterfactual Visual Alignment in MLLMs," arXiv:2606.26387, 2026. [Springer LNCS, pp. 287-305, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37232-1_16 (arXiv comment: ECCV 2026)]

method: Dense structured traces and Trace-Grounded GRPO with structured rewards.
data: Reference traces from a tri-perspective verification pipeline; Qwen3-VL-8B.
evaluation: Reasoning benchmarks; token efficiency and accuracy; baselines: prompting strategies and efficient-reasoning methods.
findings: 5.5x token efficiency and +1.3 accuracy points over Qwen3-VL.
limitations: No limitations section found (checklist text only).
reference: W. Xu, Y. Guo, K. Han, et al., "DRT: Dense Reasoning Trace for Efficient and Grounded Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2609.21675, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Mutual-information-based selection of pre-sampled descriptions, forking, and decoupled perception/reasoning rewards.
data: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct; training set with complete trajectories and descriptions.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, We-Math, M3CoT, MMStar, RealWorldQA.
findings: Fewer full trajectories needed for gains; decoupled reward resolves reward blindness (as framed by the authors).
limitations: Appendix validates MI as a quality indicator across models; no limitations section found.
reference: Y. Zhang, J. Zhao, Z. Wu, et al., "MIRL: Mutual Information-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models," arXiv:2605.01520, 2026. [Preprint]

method: VGPO: visual attention compensation and visual-focus reinforcement inside RLVR.
data: Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B; trained on Geo3K and other sizes.
evaluation: Math and general benchmarks incl. Super-CLEVR and a 448-question logic benchmark; baselines: DAPO, ThinkLite-VL-7B, VL- Rethinker-7B.
findings: Beats DAPO even in data-constrained settings.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Z. Wang, F. Xiong, L. Lin, et al., "Visually-Guided Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2604.09349, 2026. [ACL 2026 long papers, pp. 6646-6664, doi:10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.301]

method: Controlled perturbation study (misleading captions, wrong CoT) on RL-finetuned and closed models.
data: Spatial VQA sets: 3DSRBench, CV-Bench, Spatial-MM, WhatsUp.
evaluation: Accuracy, robustness and CoT consistency under perturbations; open vs closed models.
findings: Accuracy-faithfulness tradeoff: more RL steps raise headline accuracy while consistency worsens.
limitations: Calls for evaluation that goes beyond accuracy.
reference: R. Zhao, A. Shah, X. Zhu, et al., "On Robustness and Chain-of-Thought Consistency of RL-Finetuned VLMs," arXiv:2602.12506, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: ICML 2026)]

method: Visual perception reward: a judging LLM scores consistency between visual annotations taken from CoT trajectories and the response, added to the accuracy reward.
data: 1,442 training samples.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, WeMath, MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MMStar, EMMA; baseline incl. Vision-R1 (200K samples).
findings: State of the art on most benchmarks with only 1,442 samples.
limitations: Not stated as a section; needs a judge LLM (reviewer note).
reference: T. Xiao, X. Xu, Z. Huang, et al., "Perception-R1: Advancing Multimodal Reasoning Capabilities of MLLMs via Visual Perception Reward," arXiv:2506.07218, 2025. [Preprint]

contribution: Implicit perception loss, no reward model
method: PAPO: Implicit Perception Loss (KL term) plus Double Entropy Loss, plugged into GRPO/DAPO; no extra data, reward model or teacher.
data: Same training data and rewards as GRPO/DAPO baselines (names not extracted).
evaluation: Diverse multimodal benchmarks, high-vision-dependency subsets, perception-error analysis; baselines GRPO and DAPO.
findings: +4.4 to +17.5% overall; 30.5% fewer perception errors.
limitations: Authors: no scaling beyond 7B or other model families; training efficiency not optimised.
reference: Z. Wang, X. Guo, S. Stoica, et al., "Perception-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2507.06448, 2025. [Preprint]

contribution: Outcome reward after CoT cold start
method: Cold-start on a 200K multimodal CoT set, then GRPO with a hard-format result reward and Progressive Thinking Suppression Training.
data: Vision-R1-cold (200K CoT); 10K multimodal math RL set.
evaluation: Multimodal math benchmarks incl. MathVista (73.5% for 7B); ablations on thinking length.
findings: ~6% average gain; Vision-R1-7B 73.5% on MathVista.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: W. Huang, B. Jia, Z. Zhai, et al., "Vision-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in Multimodal Large Language Models," arXiv:2503.06749, 2025. [Preprint (author-stated: ICLR 2026)]

method: Verifiable perception rewards (e.g. IoU for detection) with GRPO for LVLMs.
data: Few-shot fine-grained classification, detection, reasoning grounding sets.
evaluation: COCO two-shot, LVIS, classification accuracy; baseline: SFT.
findings: +24.3% one-shot classification; +21.9 COCO two-shot.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Z. Liu, Z. Sun, Y. Zang, et al., "Visual-RFT: Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning," arXiv:2503.01785, 2025. [ICCV 2025, pp. 2034-2044, doi:10.1109/ICCV51701.2025.00197]

method: MCTS-measured difficulty selects 11K hard samples for RFT (no distillation).
data: 70K open-source examples filtered to 11K (7B) and 7.5K (72B).
evaluation: Eight visual reasoning benchmarks; MathVista 75.1 (7B); baseline: random-sample RFT.
findings: +7% average over Qwen2.5-VL-7B; beats larger models.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: X. Wang, Z. Yang, C. Feng, et al., "SoTA with Less: MCTS-Guided Sample Selection for Data-Efficient Visual Reasoning Self-Improvement," arXiv:2504.07934, 2025. [NeurIPS 2025, doi:10.52202/085713-3964 (OpenAlex record)]

method: 8B process reward model scoring steps, used for best-of-N selection; VisualPRM400K data and VisualProcessBench.
data: VisualPRM400K (automated); VisualProcessBench (2,866 samples, 26,950 step labels).
evaluation: Seven reasoning benchmarks, BoN; baselines: outcome reward models and self-consistency.
findings: +5.9 points on InternVL2.5-78B; beats outcome RMs and self-consistency.
limitations: Authors: open MLLMs rarely mark steps wrong (F1 19.2 on negative steps for InternVL2.5-8B).
reference: W. Wang, Z. Gao, L. Chen, et al., "VisualPRM: An Effective Process Reward Model for Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2503.10291, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Human-crafted visual-question pairs with control groups.
data: 346 images and 1,129 questions (abstract).
evaluation: 15 models benchmarked; question-pair accuracy 31.42% for GPT-4V, others below 16% (abstract).
findings: Failure modes: language hallucination and visual illusion.
limitations: Limitations and Future Work section present.
reference: T. Guan, F. Liu, X. Wu, et al., "HallusionBench: An Advanced Diagnostic Suite for Entangled Language Hallucination and Visual Illusion in Large Vision-Language Models," arXiv:2310.14566, 2023. [CVPR 2024, doi:10.1109/CVPR52733.2024.01363 (OpenAlex record)]

method: Literature survey with taxonomy of causes, evaluation and mitigation.
data: Not applicable (228 references, per arXiv comment).
evaluation: Reviews benchmarks and metrics (e.g. CHAIR, CCEval).
findings: Organises causes, benchmarks and mitigation strategies; lists open questions.
limitations: Predates the RL-based fixes in this review.
reference: Z. Bai, P. Wang, T. Xiao, et al., "Hallucination of Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey," arXiv:2404.18930, 2024. [Preprint]

venue_note: International Journal of Computer Vision, doi:10.1007/s11263-026-02756-9
method: Survey with a faithfulness/factuality taxonomy of hallucination, benchmarks and detection methods.
data: Not applicable.
evaluation: Summarises benchmark construction, objectives and metrics.
findings: Highlights limitations of current benchmarks and detection methods.
limitations: Survey scope is evaluation and detection, not training rewards.
reference: Z. Chen, Y. Min, J. Zhang, et al., "A Survey of Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation and Detection," arXiv:2507.19024, 2025. [International Journal of Computer Vision, doi:10.1007/s11263-026-02756-9]

contribution: Object Consistency Score reward with PPO
method: Captioning as an MDP; Object Consistency Score (F1 of object precision and recall) as reward, token-level KL regularisation, lightweight PPO with a shared frozen backbone and soft-prompt adapters.
data: COCO (CHAIR) and Visual Genome (CCEval); object lists from dataset annotations or YOLO detectors; InstructBLIP (Vicuna-7B) and LLaVA.
evaluation: CHAIRs/CHAIRi, CCEval, coverage, SPICE, BLEU, BERTScore, METEOR; baselines: InstructBLIP, mPLUG-Owl, LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT, hard prompting, LURE and other mitigation methods.
findings: Up to 41% fewer hallucinated captions on COCO and 29% on Visual Genome; caption quality kept or improved; generalises to LLaVA.
limitations: Authors: reward quality depends on object-detector accuracy; single training run per model; one day on 8 A6000 GPUs.
reference: T. Nguyen, H. S. Yoon, T. M. Luu, et al., "Metric-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Object Hallucination Reduction in LVLM-Based Image Captioning," IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 125177-125195, 2026, doi: 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3723028.

method: Process-supervised RL with a critic that scores reasoning steps (V-tableR1).
data: Seven tabular datasets including TabFact and InfoTabs; Qwen 4B model.
evaluation: Accuracy against SFT and outcome-reward baselines.
findings: Up to +10.6% over SFT.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Y. Jiang, Y. An, X. Yang, et al., "V-tableR1: Process-Supervised Multimodal Table Reasoning with Critic-Guided Policy Optimization," arXiv:2604.20755, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Position-aware diagnosis and GRPO with a rubric-based reward (PAGER) on Qwen3-VL-4B.
data: PixMo-derived captions.
evaluation: Rubric and hallucination metrics; baseline CapRL.
findings: Beats CapRL on long-caption faithfulness; benefit concentrated at later positions.
limitations: Has a "Discussion and limitations" section.
reference: Y. Hu, Z. Yang, J. Jing, et al., "Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning," arXiv:2610.31111, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: NeurIPS 2026)]

method: Witness-adjudicator reward with hypergeometric scoring for GRPO captioning (VCap), 8B model.
data: AI2D, MMStar, RealWorldQA, V*.
evaluation: Benchmark accuracy; baseline CapRL.
findings: Matches CapRL on average (66.58 vs 66.56), i.e. no clear gain.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: X. Lu, J. Wang, Y.-F. Zhang, et al., "VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning," arXiv:2605.28023, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Truth-grounded anchors with exploration in RL
venue_note: Springer LNCS, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37383-0_24 (OpenAlex record; volume not confirmed)
method: Anchor-and-explore RL (AnE) with truth-grounded anchors.
data: Eight benchmarks incl. MathVista, MathVision, MathVerse, LogicVista, ScienceQA, MMMU, EMMA.
evaluation: Accuracy per benchmark.
findings: +10.3% across eight benchmarks.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Z. Wang, Y. Zeng, Z. Gong, et al., "AnE: Pushing the Reasoning Frontier of Multimodal LLMs via Anchor Evolution," arXiv:2605.25571, 2026. [Springer LNCS, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37383-0_24 (OpenAlex record; volume not confirmed)]

method: Perceptual Flow Network: variational RL with multi-dimensional perception rewards, Qwen3-VL-8B base.
data: V*, TreeBench, MME-RealWorld-lite.
evaluation: Accuracy on three benchmarks.
findings: Gains of 13.1%, 10.4% and 21% on the three benchmarks.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Y. Li, Y. Gong, H. Zhan, et al., "Perceptual Flow Network for Visually Grounded Reasoning," arXiv:2605.02730, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: ICML 2026)]

method: Decoupled confidence calibration trained with RL (VL-Calibration).
data: 13 benchmarks.
evaluation: Accuracy, ECE and AUROC.
findings: ECE 0.421 to 0.098; accuracy +2.3 to +3.0%.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: W. Xiao, X. Xu, and L. Gan, "VL-Calibration: Decoupled Confidence Calibration for Large Vision-Language Models Reasoning," arXiv:2604.09529, 2026. [ACL 2026 long papers, pp. 44791-44815, doi:10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.2074]

method: Iterative evidence refinement trained with GRPO (SIEVE) on Qwen3-VL-4B/8B.
data: MME-Real-Lite, RealWorldQA, MathVista, LogicVista, WeMath, a hallucination benchmark.
evaluation: Accuracy per benchmark.
findings: Improves visual reasoning and hallucination scores over the base models.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Z. Shi, K. Mei, Y. Quan, et al., "Improving Visual Reasoning with Iterative Evidence Refinement," arXiv:2603.14117, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Perception-aware RL objective (GPRO).
data: Five benchmarks.
evaluation: Accuracy and response length.
findings: MathVista +6.0%; MathVerse +1.8% with responses 51.5% shorter.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: X. Diao, Z. Liu, C. Zhang, et al., "Addressing Overthinking in Large Vision-Language Models via Gated Perception- Reasoning Optimization," arXiv:2601.04442, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: ACL 2026)]

method: Contrastive Perception Policy Optimization (CPPO).
data: Agent and perception benchmarks (names not extracted).
evaluation: Average accuracy.
findings: Average gains of +11.2% and +5.9%.
limitations: Limitations appendix present.

data: Reward-modelling and tool-use benchmarks.

limitations: No limitations section found (broader-impact section only).

method: On-policy RL with fine-grained rewards against object hallucination.
data: AMBER and related benchmarks; Qwen3.6-27B used as judge.
evaluation: AMBER metrics; judge-model scores.
findings: Reduces hallucination without shortening captions.
limitations: Limitations appendix present.
reference: X. Long, J. Zhang, Y. Min, et al., "Beyond Saying Less: Fine-Grained Alignment for Informative and Faithful Vision- Language Models," arXiv:2609.35294, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Think with Structured Grounding: perceptual RL without external tools (TwSG).
data: Chart and table benchmarks.
evaluation: Average accuracy.
findings: 73.70% average accuracy.
limitations: States a limitation: only models of 8B or smaller tested.
reference: C. Jiang, Q. Zhao, L. Xin, et al., "Think with Structured Grounding: Perceptual Reinforcement Learning for Chart and Visual- Tabular Understanding," arXiv:2608.22429, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Refusal-calibrated GRPO for generalized referring expression comprehension.
data: gRefCOCO and related no-target sets.
evaluation: Precision, AP.
findings: Precision 45.0 to 62.2 (AP 26.4 to 34.0) in one setting; 53.5 to 60.5 on gRefCOCO.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: X. Yang, J. Ling, T. Huang, et al., "Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO," arXiv:2608.04698, 2026. [Preprint]

method: ConsistRoll: cross-view consistency inside GRPO and Hint-GRPO, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 3B.
data: Math-and-logic, general understanding and hallucination-sensitive evaluations (names not extracted).
evaluation: Benchmark accuracy.
findings: Improves both GRPO and Hint-GRPO on both model sizes.
limitations: Limitations appendix (E) present.
reference: X. Zou, H. Deng, Y. Yan, et al., "Consistency as Inductive Bias: Learning Cross-View Invariance for Robust Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2606.29812, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Analysis of GRPO with an IoU reward and label-free stopping rules, Qwen3-VL-4B.
data: About 2,400 training samples; single-object referring expression comprehension.
evaluation: Acc@0.5 (79.6% single-shot base).

reference: A. Tripathy and A. Krishnan, "Iterative Visual Thinking and the Self-Correction Mirage in VLM Grounding," arXiv:2606.13156, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Reinforcement learning with robust rubric rewards (RLR3), deterministic verification of rubrics generated by frontier models.
data: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B; 15 benchmarks; ViRL, DeepVision, OpenMMR training sets.
evaluation: Macro-average accuracy; controlled audits of the verifier.
findings: +4.7 points over the base model and above RLVR.
limitations: Limitations stated: rubrics depend on an external frontier model; smaller margin on OpenMMR (visual puzzles).

method: RL that learns from successful trajectories under corrupted images, Qwen3-VL 4B/8B.
data: About 30K training samples; seven benchmarks (MathVista, WeMath, ChartQA, LogicVista, MMStar, VisualPuzzles, RealWorldQA).
evaluation: Accuracy on clean, seen-corruption and unseen-corruption inputs; baseline GRPO.
findings: Robustness +2.4% (seen) and +2.3% (unseen) over GRPO, clean accuracy matched.

reference: R. Liu, D. Yu, H. Liu, et al., "Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning Against Visual Degradation," arXiv:2605.09262, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Rule-based spatial reward in GRPO for multi-
method: Compositional Grounded Contrast (CGC): multi-image instances built from single-image grounding annotations plus a rule- based spatial reward inside GRPO (Think-before-Grounding).
data: MIG-Bench and VLM2-Bench; transfer to MathVista, MuirBench, MMStar, MMMU, BLINK; Qwen3-VL-8B base.
evaluation: Benchmark accuracy against strong baselines.
findings: State of the art on MIG-Bench and VLM2-Bench; +2.90 MathVista, +2.88 MuirBench, +1.93 MMStar over the base model.
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: L. Zheng, Z. Shao, Y. Zhou, et al., "CGC: Compositional Grounded Contrast for Fine-Grained Multi-Image Understanding," arXiv:2604.22498, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Warm-start on faithful samples before RL
method: Faithful Warm-Start (FWS): build FaithfulQA by curating samples with explicit vision-language causal links from six general VQA sets, filter with a VLM judge, warm-start the policy, then apply RL.
data: FaithfulQA (derived from six general VQA benchmarks, e.g. ChartQA, AI2D, ScienceQA); Qwen3-VL backbone.
evaluation: General VQA benchmarks plus a section analysing reasoning faithfulness (4.3); baselines are the base model and RL without warm-start (as read in the headings and abstract).
findings: Warm-starting toward faithful reasoning before RL stabilises training and improves grounded answers (authors).
limitations: Only a Future Work section; no limitations section. Depends on a VLM judge to purify the data.
reference: P. Gao, Y. Lee, Y. Zhang, et al., "Be Faithful When Response: Returning Fluent and Grounded Answers for Vision-Language Models Reinforcement Learning," arXiv:2606.29984, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Step-level reward model with fine-grained RL
method: Chain of Step (CoS) structured reasoning; ShareGPT-Step-300K with step labels from Monte Carlo estimation and LLM-as- judge; step-level process reward model; iterative DPO and GRPO with fine-grained rewards; test-time step beam search.
data: ShareGPT-Step-300K (built by the authors); public vision-language reasoning benchmarks.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, MMStar, ChartQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA and others; Qwen2-VL / InternVL / LLaVA backbones; ablations on reasoning pattern and GRPO variant.
findings: Fine-grained step rewards give consistent gains and enable inference-time scaling (authors).
limitations: Appendix G: process labels from Monte Carlo and LLM judge are not guaranteed correct; annotation noise remains.
reference: H. Chen, X. Lou, X. Feng, et al., "Unveiling Chain of Step Reasoning for Vision-Language Models with Fine-grained Rewards," arXiv:2509.19003, 2025. [Preprint (author-stated: NeurIPS 2025)]

contribution: Rule-based rewards from verified caption errors
method: Perception RL: extract verified errors from dense captions and convert them into QA pairs with fixed labels and rule-based rewards (chain and multiple-choice QA); Perception Agentic RL for fine-grained cases with Python tools; DAPO training.
data: Pipeline-generated perception QA; Qwen3-VL backbone.
evaluation: MMStar, RealWorldQA, V* and other perception benchmarks; comparison with specialised tool-use models; ablation of the two construction routes.
findings: Verifiable perception rewards improve perception benchmarks beyond answer-only RL (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found; scattered mentions only.
reference: T. Guan, Z. Yang, M. Yang, et al., "PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions," arXiv:2610.37471, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Exact-match reward for finding an injected
method: Proxy task: inject one subtle synthetic error into a 200-word human caption and train the VLM to localise the corrupted span, with a binary exact-match reward (GRPO). Also releases ViCrit-Bench for hallucination-type diagnosis.
data: Captions with injected errors; ViCrit-Bench (images across domains, annotated hallucination categories).
evaluation: Reports gains on MathVista, MathVerse, MMMU, MMHal, CHAIR, MMStar, MM-Vet; Qwen2.5-VL-7B and larger models; benchmarks open and proprietary VLMs on ViCrit-Bench.
findings: Training on the proxy task transfers to perception and reasoning benchmarks and to hallucination metrics (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: X. Wang, Z. Yang, C. Feng, et al., "ViCrit: A Verifiable Reinforcement Learning Proxy Task for Visual Perception in VLMs," arXiv:2506.10128, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Repair erroneous trajectories to build token/step-level masks (Difference Feedback), injected into GRPO (DF-GRPO) and PPO (DF-PPO) without step annotations.
data: Model-repaired trajectories; Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B/72B and InternVL backbones.
evaluation: MMStar, MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, AI2D; matched compute budgets; GRPO, GSPO, DAPO and PPO baselines.
findings: About 3% average improvement under matched compute (authors).
limitations: Section 6: misaligned minimal edits and dependence on the repair model producing correct short edits.
reference: Feiding, Y. Zhang, Y. Liao, et al., "Difference Feedback: Generating Multimodal Process-Level Supervision for VLM Reinforcement Learning," arXiv:2603.27482, 2026. [Preprint]

contribution: Outcome-reward agentic RL with image zoom
method: End-to-end agentic RL (no cold-start SFT) where the model calls its own grounding as an image-zoom tool; reward design and data selection tailored to tool use.
data: Curated training data (appendix B); Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
evaluation: V*, HR-Bench, MME-RealWorld, POPE, MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, WeMath, LogicVista, DynaMath; ablations and tool-use dynamics.
findings: Gains on perception, grounding, hallucination and maths; tool-use evolves from exploration to efficient use (authors).
limitations: Appendix E: shortcuts remain (shallow reasoning, imprecise localisation); only Qwen2.5-VL tested.
reference: Z. Zheng, M. Yang, J. Hong, et al., "DeepEyes: Incentivizing "Thinking with Images" via Reinforcement Learning," arXiv:2505.14362, 2025. [Preprint (author-stated: ICLR 2026)]

short: Ground What You See (Pan et al.)
method: Plan-and-caption stage with a quality-based caption reward; reward-variance-guided sample selection; NTK-based conflict- aware regularisation (GRPO).
data: Open multimodal training data; InternVL-family backbones.
evaluation: POPE, MMBench, MathVista, ChartQA, hallucination benchmarks; ablations of the three modules.
findings: Reduces hallucination during RL and improves benchmark accuracy (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: M. Pan, W. Gan, J. Chen, et al., "Ground What You See: Hallucination-Resistant MLLMs via Caption Feedback, Diversity- Aware Sampling, and Conflict Regularization," arXiv:2601.06224, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: AAAI-2026 poster)]

method: MCTS-guided GRPO producing dense step-level rewards without annotation, interleaved with SFT to fix cold start; a PRM for test-time search.
data: Seven benchmarks, four VLM backbones; self-generated MCTS data.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVision, DynaMath and others; Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and others; compared with SFT and GRPO baselines.
findings: Gains across seven benchmarks and four backbones over SFT and GRPO (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Y. Jiang, C. Lei, Y. Ding, et al., "PROPA: Toward Process-level Optimization in Visual Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning," arXiv:2511.10279, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Compositional consistency audit, then sequence-level RL with a structured reward built from anchored factual and temporal claims parsed from captions.
data: Caption-derived structured units; Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL.
evaluation: MME, MVBench, Video-MME, TempCompass and hallucination tests; ablation study.
findings: Structured consistency rewards improve grounding and general video benchmarks (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: Y. Quan, Z. Shi, J. Zhao, et al., "Reinforcing Consistency in Video MLLMs with Structured Rewards," arXiv:2604.01460, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: COLM 2026)]

method: AutoRubric: self-aggregation of reasoning checkpoints from successful trajectories into problem-specific rubrics; an LLM judge scores rubrics; combined with outcome reward in GRPO.
data: Training problems with automatically collected rubrics; Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, WeMath, MMMU-Pro; dedicated faithfulness evaluation; ablations and training dynamics.
findings: State-of-the-art on six benchmarks and better reasoning faithfulness (authors).
limitations: Limitations section: the judge adds about 40% training time per step.
reference: M. Jia, Z. Zhang, I. Cases, et al., "AutoRubric: Rubric-Based Generative Rewards for Faithful Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2510.14738, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Structured CoT that models 3D perception, multi-objective process rewards and segment-wise advantage estimation (GRPO variant); SCOUT-24k dataset.
data: SCOUT-24k (authors, synthesised); Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B.
evaluation: CV-Bench, SpatialBench, 3DSRBench, VSI-Bench; out-of-domain evaluation and ablations.
findings: Better spatial reasoning with process rewards (authors).
limitations: Appendix: only 3B and 7B models; datasets rely on bounding-box style annotations.
reference: Z. Zhou, H. Yuan, W. Zhang, et al., "SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward," arXiv:2608.12220, 2026. [Preprint]

method: Self-rewarding step-level confidence signals (textual and cross-modal), SFT warm-up for confidence expression, then RL with several reward functions for calibration.
data: Reasoning-chain annotated data (section 4.2).
evaluation: Multimodal reasoning datasets; calibration metrics; baselines listed in 4.4; component ablations.
findings: Better step-level confidence calibration and fewer snowballed errors (authors).
limitations: Limitation section: relies on internal states and uncertainty estimates to assess confidence.
reference: Z. He, S. Polisetty, Z. Fan, et al., "MMBoundary: Advancing MLLM Knowledge Boundary Awareness through Reasoning Step Confidence Calibration," arXiv:2505.23224, 2025. [Preprint (author-stated: ACL 2025)]

method: Positive, counterfactual and random-masking training; language-guided evidence region construction (DeFacto-100K); GRPO with three rewards for answer, structure and evidence selection.
data: DeFacto-100K (authors); DeFacto-1.5K human-annotated benchmark.
evaluation: MMMU, POPE, MMStar, V*, VSR, ChartQA, DocVQA, OCRBench, AI2D and others; Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B.
findings: Improves evidence-grounded consistency beyond accuracy (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found; an impact statement only.
reference: T. Xu, H. Jing, Y. Li, et al., "DeFacto: Counterfactual Thinking with Images for Enforcing Evidence-Grounded and Faithful Reasoning," arXiv:2509.20912, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Token-level saliency maps via logits decomposition; reward = overlap between saliency and human-annotated boxes; GRPO.
data: Public VQA training data with box annotations; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
evaluation: MMMU, POPE, MME, MMStar, MMBench, MME-RealWorld, VSR, ChartQA, DocVQA and others; faithfulness of saliency maps evaluated separately.
findings: Improves faithfulness and interpretability and general VQA (authors).
limitations: Section 5 Limitation and Conclusion (heading present).
reference: S. Gong, M. Hu, Q. Zhang, et al., "Saliency-R1: Enforcing Interpretable and Faithful Vision-language Reasoning via Saliency- map Alignment Reward," arXiv:2604.04500, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: CVPR 2026)]

method: Hallucination-as-Cue analysis: modality-specific corruptions that remove information needed for the answer, used in training and inference (GRPO).
data: Standard RL post-training data with corruptions; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, WeMath, CLEVR-type tests; analysis settings and model scaling.
findings: Training on corrupted (hallucination-inducing) data can still improve reasoning, which questions how much RL uses the image (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: G. Zhang, J. Peng, Z. Tan, et al., "Understanding the Role of Hallucination in Reinforcement Post-Training of Multimodal Reasoning Models," arXiv:2604.03179, 2026. [Preprint (author-stated: CVPR 2026)]

contribution: Tool-aware dense rewards on tool inputs and
method: Faithfulness protocol that checks whether visual tool outputs contain the queried evidence; Tool-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO) adds dense rewards on tool inputs and outputs to GRPO.
data: Visual-search and reasoning data with code-based tools; Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B.
evaluation: V*, HR-Bench, MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, MME, CharXiv; faithful tool-use rate; ablations.
findings: Higher faithful tool-use rate and accuracy than prior visual agents (authors).
limitations: Limitations section: static judge model adds cost; judge design limits.
reference: X. Hou, S. Xu, M. Biyani, et al., "CodeV: Code with Images for Faithful Visual Reasoning via Tool-Aware Policy Optimization," arXiv:2511.19661, 2025. [Preprint]

method: PEARL: derive a perception checklist of verifiable sub-questions per item; auxiliary perception rollouts give a perceptual reward and act as a fidelity gate on the reasoning reward (GRPO/DAPO).
data: Automatically derived perception probes; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, RealWorldQA, WeMath, LogicVista, DynaMath; ablation on lambda; statistical dependence of reasoning on perception.
findings: Gains over vanilla RLVR; reasoning success depends on perception probes (authors).
limitations: Section 7: extractable probes per source question are limited.
reference: C. Zhang, H. Qiu, Q. Zhang, et al., "Perceptual-Evidence Anchored Reinforced Learning for Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2511.18437, 2025. [Preprint]

contribution: Reflective policy optimisation with visual re-
method: Balanced Reflective Policy Optimization (BRPO) to decide when to reflect on the image; visual re-attention by re-supplying tokens during reflection or at test time.
data: Cold-start data in appendix B; Qwen2.5-VL 7B/32B.
evaluation: MathVision, MMMU, POPE, CHAIR, MME, MMStar, MMBench, MMMU-Pro; inference-time overhead; ablations.
findings: Fewer hallucinations and better accuracy with vision-text reflection (authors).
limitations: Section 6 Limitations: the analysis assumes neglect of visual information is a main cause.
reference: X. Chu, X. Chen, G. Wang, et al., "Qwen Look Again: Guiding Vision-Language Reasoning Models to Re-attention Visual Information," arXiv:2505.23558, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Visual Rationale Learning (ViRL): process supervision with ground-truth rationales, step-level reward shaping, and fine-grained credit assignment (PPO/DAPO-style RL).
data: Process-grounded dataset built by the authors (appendix B); Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
evaluation: POPE, MME, MMStar, V*, HR-Bench, GQA and others; baselines in 4.2; ablation and further analysis.
findings: More effective visual actions and higher perception accuracy (authors).
limitations: Appendix F: small dataset focused on perception-driven reasoning.
reference: C. Wang, H. Wang, X. Chen, et al., "From Illusion to Intention: Visual Rationale Learning for Vision-Language Reasoning," arXiv:2511.23031, 2025. [Preprint]

method: Structured process reward on GRPO scoring belief update, evidence acquisition and adaptive focus control at the action level; TRACER-Bench.
data: TRACER-Bench (authors) and public benchmarks.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, HallusionBench, MME, MMStar, RealWorldQA, MME-RealWorld; process-credit validation; ablations; Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL.
findings: Improves fragmented visual evidence tasks on public and new benchmarks (authors).
limitations: Appendix G: only open-source models at moderate scale.
reference: T. Guo, J. Leng, H. Li, et al., "CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning," arXiv:2605.16416, 2026. [Preprint]

short: Learning When to Look (Yang et al.)
method: Disentangled SFT curriculum (text-only reasoning first, then perception-grounded CoT), then RL with a pivotal-perception reward that teaches when to look.
data: Curriculum SFT data and RL data; Qwen2.5-VL-type backbone.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, HallusionBench, MME, MMStar, MMBench, WeMath, LogicVista, DynaMath, MM-Vet; behaviour analysis; ablations.
findings: Better long-chain visual reasoning and perception benchmarks (authors).
limitations: No limitations section found.
reference: S. Yang, Z. Gao, H. Qiu, et al., "Learning When to Look: A Disentangled Curriculum for Strategic Perception in Multimodal Reasoning," arXiv:2512.17227, 2025. [Preprint]

contribution: Caption model rewarded by external reasoner
method: RAPID decouples perception (MLLM writes detailed captions) from reasoning (external text-only LLM); Visual Perception Optimization (VPO) rewards the MLLM by the correctness of the external reasoner answer (GRPO).
data: Caption and QA training data; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B/72B and others.
evaluation: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, MME, MMBench, WeMath, LogicVista, DynaMath, MM-Vet, SEED; caption quality; cost analysis; generalisation across MLLMs.
findings: Faithful, query-relevant captions that transfer across reasoners and MLLMs (authors).
limitations: Appendix A: no auto-thinking switch; architecture is domain-specific in its current design.
reference: Y. Gou, K. Chen, Z. Liu, et al., "Reasoning-Aligned Perception Decoupling for Scalable Multi-modal Reasoning," arXiv:2506.04559, 2025. [Preprint (author-stated: ICLR 2026)]
